EpisodeOrderRequest.description:
Full ordered list of a series' episode (sermon) ids for a bulk reorder.

Ceiling: ``MAX_PAGE_SIZE`` ids. The drag client assembles this list from
``GET /sermons?series_id=``, which is itself capped at ``MAX_PAGE_SIZE`` per
page, and this endpoint requires the *complete* ordered set — so a series
with more episodes than that cannot be reordered through the portal at all.
Reordering a >``MAX_PAGE_SIZE``-episode series is out of scope for this
batch; the cap makes that limit an explicit 422 rather than a silent
partial write.

`week_start` is the Monday (UTC) that opens the bucket; `count` is the

sermons fell in that week. Reach, not engagement — the word "plays" does
not belong on this series.

SermonAdminDetail.description:
Staff-facing detail. Mirrors the `SermonAdminListItem` split: the editor
screen's "saved N min ago" stamp needs a server-side `updated_at` baseline,
which the public `SermonDetail` (anonymous `/catalog/sermons/{id}`) must
not carry.

`tier` keeps the inherited meaning — the *resolved* effective tier (sermon
tier, else series tier, else free), same as `SermonDetail`. The editor
screen also needs the raw column to drive the tier radio, so that is a
separate field: `tier_override` is `Sermon.tier` verbatim — NULL when the
sermon inherits from its series (or the free default), otherwise the
explicit choice. Reassigning `tier`'s meaning in a subclass was an LSP trap
that the Series/Announcements editors would have cloned.
SermonAdminDetail.title: SermonAdminDetail

SubscriptionAdminItem.description:
One row of the staff-facing subscriptions read (plan §A.3, §W20).

A staff-readable enumeration of the paying membership: `Subscription`
joined to `User` for `user_name` / `user_email`. Manager+ only, paginated.

Deliberately carries **no** monetary field — no `amount`, `price`,
`currency` or MRR (resolved decision 2). No amount is stored on
`Subscription` and the webhook never parses one; there is nothing truthful
to put here and Phase 2 shows no dollar figure anywhere in the portal.
`current_period_end` is the model's `valid_until` column (null on free /
fully-lapsed rows). `provider_customer_id` is null until the member's first
payment lands via webhook — the frontend hides "Open in Stripe" when it is.
SubscriptionAdminItem.title: SubscriptionAdminItem

SubscriptionCounts.description:

toast, not a second one written for this screen. `monthly` / `annual` split
that same population (paid tier, `status IN (active, cancelled)`) by tier,
so `active_paid == monthly + annual` holds by construction.

UserActiveResponse.description:
The updated account, plus a flag set when a Redis outage forced
refresh-token revocation to be deferred (plan §W18, GATE 6 = commit-first).
Set on **deactivation** when the lockout committed but the token revoke could
not be recorded, and on **reactivation** when the best-effort revoke of any
still-live pre-deactivation refresh token could not be recorded (CWE-613).
The state change still committed and every request re-checks `is_active`, so
the flag only tells an operator a Redis-backed revoke did not land.
UserActiveResponse.title: UserActiveResponse

put.description:
Bulk atomic reorder of a series' episodes.

Body is the full ordered list of the series' episode (sermon) ids. Every id
must be an episode of this series and the set must be exactly the current
episode set — otherwise 422, naming what is wrong. Episodes are renumbered
``1..N`` by position. An episode in ``pending_review`` / ``under_review`` is
a fixed point: if the new order would change its number the whole request is
refused with 409, naming the locked episode(s). All rows are written in one
transaction or none. Returns the reordered ``{id, episode_number}`` list.

Ceiling: at most ``MAX_PAGE_SIZE`` (100) ids. The drag client sources the
full episode set from ``GET /sermons?series_id=``, which pages at
``MAX_PAGE_SIZE``, and this endpoint needs the complete ordered list — so a
series with more episodes than that cannot be reordered through the portal.
That is out of scope for this batch; the cap turns it into an explicit 422
rather than a silent partial write.

schema.title: Response Reorder Episode Order Api V1 Series  Series Id  Episode Order Put

patch.description:
Deactivate (`is_active=false`) or reactivate a staff account.

Managers may act on editors only; admins on anyone, except where it would
leave zero active admins (409). Deactivation commits first, then revokes
refresh tokens best-effort: a Redis outage still returns 200 with
`revocation_deferred=true` rather than 503, because every request re-checks
`is_active` regardless (plan §W18, GATE 6).

post.description:
Re-issue the invite for a staff account that has not finished
set-password. Same authz as `PATCH /users/{id}/active`. A 409 means the
account has already been activated (nothing to resend); a 503 means the
single-use invite jti could not be recorded (Redis down) — unlike
deactivate, this operation cannot degrade gracefully without it.

get.description:
Is the process up? Deliberately checks nothing external — a database
blip must not cause the orchestrator to kill healthy containers.
Can this instance serve traffic? Checks critical dependencies.
